# Flat entrance door maintenance request

## Case details

- property: 14 Lantern Mews, Brindlewick, ZZ1 1ZZ

## Initial request
The paint on the inside of my flat entrance door is flaking, and the door has started catching near the top. Could someone inspect it and let me know what can be done?

## Attachments
- fire-door-quotation.pdf

input.message:
Hello Ms Vale — an update on your entrance door (reported 3 February).

Where things stand: the decorator attended on 7 February as agreed and inspected the door visually only (event-010). He has quoted for sanding, filling and repainting the flat-side face and visible top edge. That quotation is with your landlord for a decision, and it does not include adjusting the door or its hinges, so it would not by itself stop the door catching at the top (event-011, event-016).

Your questions: repainting the flat-side face would not change how the door operates — it is surface work only. Separately, because this is a fire-resisting flat entrance door and it currently needs a firm pull to latch, we are arranging for the closing/latching to be looked at properly with the building manager before any work is booked.

In the meantime, please keep closing the door firmly each time so it latches fully, and do not wedge or prop it open. Tell us straight away if it stops latching at all, or if you see damage to the edge, frame or seals.

No visit is booked. Nothing will be arranged without agreeing a window with you in advance, after 10:00, as you asked (event-003, event-009). Your request that personal items are not photographed is on the file and will be passed to any attending contractor (event-009).

handover.gap: Whether the top-edge contact and slow closing affect the door's fire performance cannot be established from any record: no door schedule, no certification, no measured clearances, and the only attendance was a decorator's visual look. Building management has not answered the 12 Feb scope query. VAT treatment of the £186.00 is not stated on the quotation.
options: Instruct a competent fire-door inspector (FDIS or equivalent) to survey the door set and report, after obtaining a price and the landlord's approval, and consult Brindlewick Court first — resolves the fire-safety question but adds cost and delay.

Ask Brindlewick Court building management to inspect or confirm responsibility for the fire door as part of the block's fire-door regime (Fire Safety (England) Regulations 2022 checks) before any landlord spend — may be the correct cost owner but depends on their response time.

Approve the £186.00 decorating work alone once building management confirms no objection — the tenant's paint complaint is resolved but the catching/latching defect on a fire door is left unaddressed; not recommended as a standalone outcome.
handover.recommended: Chase Brindlewick Court for the block's fire-door inspection position (option 2) and in parallel obtain a price for an independent fire-door inspection for the landlord's decision (option 1); hold the decorating work until the door operation is settled, so any adjustment happens before repainting.
